market_question: Ukraine agrees not to join NATO before 2027?
reasoning: Ukraine's government and public overwhelmingly back eventual NATO membership; a public pledge not to join would be politically toxic and is contradicted by consistent official statements. While peace negotiations could theoretically force such a concession, the current military and diplomatic situation makes a formal neutrality agreement before 2027 unlikely. Thus the market-implied 17% probability significantly overstates the true chance.
evidence_points: Polling consistently shows >80% of Ukrainians support joining NATO post-2022 invasion.
President Zelenskyy and senior officials have repeatedly ruled out neutrality as a concession, instead seeking security guarantees and membership.
No active peace talks are underway that would produce such a binding agreement in the near term, and Russia's demands remain maximalist.
sources_consulted: Kyiv International Institute of Sociology polls on NATO (2023-2024)
Zelenskyy's statements at NATO Vilnius Summit 2023 and subsequent press conferences
Coverage of peace negotiation dynamics by Reuters and Associated Press (2023-2024)
